title: New license request: Autonomous Commons Dedication 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 (ACD-1.0 / ACD-1.1 / ACD-1.2)
body:
**License Name**
Autonomous Commons Dedication, versions 1.0, 1.1 and 1.2 (ACD-1.0, ACD-1.1, ACD-1.2). Each version is a separate, frozen text: its bytes are pinned by SHA-256 in the repository and will not change. One rule per version is requested. Suggested keys: `acd-1.0`, `acd-1.1`, `acd-1.2`.

**License Homepage URL**
- ACD-1.0: https://yutapr0117-design.github.io/portfolio/LICENSES/ACD-1.0.txt
- ACD-1.1: https://yutapr0117-design.github.io/portfolio/LICENSES/ACD-1.1.txt
- ACD-1.2: https://yutapr0117-design.github.io/portfolio/LICENSES/ACD-1.2.txt

**Reference URLs**
- Pins of the frozen texts: https://github.com/yutapr0117-design/portfolio/blob/main/LICENSES/FROZEN.md
- Repository that applies ACD-1.0: https://github.com/yutapr0117-design/portfolio (see `LICENSE`, which carries `SPDX-License-Identifier: ACD-1.0`)

**License Notes**
- **What it is:** a public-domain dedication (Section 3) plus a separate, unconditional permissive licence (Section 4). The licence does not depend on the dedication being valid. It also has an explicit patent licence (Section 8). It places no conditions on recipients: no attribution, no notice, no share-alike. The closest existing keys are probably `cc0-1.0` and `unlicense`. 1.1 and 1.2 are revisions of 1.0 with the same structure; 1.1 and 1.2 renumber some clauses relative to 1.0.
- **Why this is requested:** without a rule, ScanCode 32.5.0 matches these texts in fragments. In ACD-1.0 and ACD-1.1, one fragment is reported as `proprietary-license`, via `proprietary-license_544.RULE`, on a phrase in Section 6.1 that grants permission ("for any purpose, commercial or non-commercial"). With `scancode.api.get_licenses`, the `detected_license_expression` for ACD-1.0 is `public-domain AND proprietary-license AND unknown AND warranty-disclaimer AND unknown-license-reference AND unknown-spdx`. ACD-1.2 rewords that phrase, so its detection no longer includes `proprietary-license`, but it is still matched in fragments (`public-domain AND unknown AND warranty-disclaimer AND unknown-license-reference AND unknown-spdx`). A full-text rule per version would let each text be identified as one licence.
- **Status, stated plainly:** none of these versions is on the SPDX License List or OSI-approved. ACD-1.0 was posted for discussion on OSI `license-discuss`, which is not an approval submission. Its only use today is the steward's own repository. If that is below your bar for adding a licence, that is understood.
- **Disclosure:** this account belongs to the licence steward. The licence texts were drafted by an AI model (Claude) on the steward's direction. This request was written and filed by the same AI assistant, at the steward's request.
